guidance: A two-team race on win-loss records only. It does not convert ties, overtime losses or points tables, and it does not know about head-to-head results beyond the tiebreaker you choose.
method: Games behind compares won-loss difference, not raw wins: games behind = ((first wins - second wins) + (second losses - first losses)) / 2, so a leading team is zero games behind itself and is shown as a dash. Winning percentage is wins / (wins + losses) and is reported to three decimals, or as a dash when no games have been played. The most wins a team can still reach is its wins plus its remaining games. The magic number is second wins + second games left - first wins + 1: it counts combined first-team wins and second-team losses after which the second team, even winning every remaining game, cannot finish with more wins than the first team already has. The one is dropped when the first team would win a tiebreaker, because finishing level is then enough, and kept when the second team would win one. The elimination number is the same count read from the chasing side. A magic number of zero or less means the first team has clinched, a total of zero games left means the season is complete, and a negative games behind means the second team leads, in which case no magic number is reported for the first team. Wins, losses and games left are whole numbers from 0 to 199, team names are trimmed and limited to 24 characters, and a tiebreaker must be one of the three listed values. The model reads win-loss records only: ties, overtime losses, points systems and goal-difference tables are not converted, it assumes these two teams are the only contenders, and it treats an unplayed game as half a win and half a loss, so unequal games played can mislead. It keeps no schedule and stores nothing. The calculation runs entirely in the browser with no uploads, accounts or network access.
